newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch, Bertelsmann said near digital pact.
newsitem.headline: Kirch, Bertelsmann said near digital pact.

text.p: Rival German media companies Kirch Group and Bertelsmann AG are close to settling their differences over decoder systems for digital television, government sources said on Tuesday.
Leo Kirch is under pressure to find a partner for his DF1 digital station following last week's decision by Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB not to take a stake in DF1.
"There has been a certain movement between Kirch and Bertelsmann on unifying their decoder systems," a government source said.
Another government source who also asked not to be identified said an announcement involving the two and France's Canal Plus could be made soon.

The three are partners in analogue pay-TV broadcaster Premiere. Kirch and Bertelsmann had been discussing digital TV until last year, when a failure to agree on a decoder standard led Kirch to strike out on his own.

The rapprochement could also involve Deutsche Telekom AG , the second government official said. Telekom's previous refusal to endorse Kirch's decoder technology had been one of the obstacles to the distribution of DF1 via Telekom's cable television network.
"This is a typical issue where the government does not need to involve itself at all," the second official said. "Equipment questions today are best decided by the market."
A Bertelsmann spokesman said he was unaware of any change in the situation, but that he expected the two would reach an agreement by summer. Kirch officials declined to comment.
While retaining his stake in Premiere, Kirch founded Bavaria-based digital broadcaster DF1 as a rival, but legal challenges and sluggish sales could now be forcing him back into Bertelsmann's arms.

Last week, Premiere warned that the entire digital pay TV industry in Germany could fail unless DF1 and Premiere reached some form of cooperation agreement sharing DF1's digital platform and Premiere's customers.
Premiere has launched a digital pilot project with some 30,000 of its subscribers and believes that thousands more would be willing to trade their analogue service for digital services.

There has been speculation that Canal Plus could sell Kirch its stake in Premiere in exchange for Kirch's stake in Telepiu, an Italian pay TV group. Bertelsmann officials say this is not likely to happen and say they could veto any such move.
Premiere won a major skirmish with Kirch in February, when a court blocked DF1 from advertising outside its home state of Bavaria.
Kirch owns 25 percent of Premiere and has been the channel's main supplier of feature films. Bertelsmann and Canal Plus each hold 37.5 percent of the station.

Digital technology allows broadcasters to squeeze more channels into cable and satellite networks and to show films in CD-like quality. It also allows new media forms such as video on demand, home-shopping and possibly interactive games.
